Another photon of wavelength $540\text{ nm}$ collides with an isolated stationary electron.

Explain why it is not possible for the deflected photon to have a wavelength less than $540\text{ nm}$.

stem:
A photon of wavelength $540\text{ nm}$ collides with an isolated stationary electron, as illustrated in Fig. 11.1.

{{figure:figure_11_1.png}}

The photon is deflected elastically by the electron.
The wavelength of the deflected photon is $544\text{ nm}$.
